name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.203.0 — Genesis gains the DESIGN_BRIEF state after the zero-day gate is green: a web host now writes docs/design/brief.md and fills the host's rules tables under Fable, catalog-inventory.js derives the installed catalog inventory the driver verifies mechanically, a design-brief skill and brief/paths templates ship the workbench, design-contract-check.js gains overrides for the new state, and the gray mock app stops auto-picking the stack or skipping the scaffold — genesis always picks and scaffolds, reading the mock app's approval record for the last time at this state's entry. 7.202.0 — Gates, per workspace: /spec:enforce now discovers and wires enforcers once per workspace, not once per repo — a new workspace-scan.js walks the tree for package manifests, the enforce cell grammar gains workspace (and, for naming, a layer of code/schema/routes/wire), and the grounding contract's Rule enforcement section states the (workspace x stack x category) entry shape and id grammar; a monorepo with a Python API and a TypeScript frontend now gets its own checker set per workspace, with naming enforced per layer from the host naming table, and every checker wired to run from its own workspace root inside the one gate string. 7.201.0 — The design contract is code: a host with a UI stack now declares design: {kit, tokens, rules} in its grounding config instead of a single app pointer, and design-contract-check.js is the mechanical presence oracle — it walks the kit directory for intent-named composites, parses the rules file's intent-to-pattern and per-layer naming tables, and reports every gap by kind and remedy. /spec:init locates the three paths and seeds the rules file from a template when absent, running the check as an advisory report rather than a gate; /spec:doctor check 8 runs the same script; /spec:enforce gains the kit-discipline category (folding color/typography/density out of the old forbidden-symbol/structural-pattern split) so a host's kit-backed design rules get a real discovered enforcer alongside everything else. No doctrine prose enforces any of this — the check script and the taxonomy are the only oracles.
